mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate increase (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 monthly increases triggers a confidence effect that accelerates S&P 500 gains over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive after controlling for lagged S&P 500 volatility (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 104) followed by a rebound above 104 indicates a turning point that reduces near-term uncertainty and supports S&P 500 upward momentum over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses below 104 then crosses above 104 within the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns show no significant correlation with the INDPRO turning point (Spearman's rho < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of contracting consumer demand (RSAFS < 450,000) reduce capacity utilization, lowering growth expectations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS crosses below 450,000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative when demand is contracting (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS by at least 1% in the same month creates a dual signal of deflationary pressure and tighter policy, which predicts negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < previous and FEDFUNDS < previous by >=1%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both triggers are present (multivariate regression p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment (UNRATE > 5.5%) over three months indicates weakening labor market strength, which is associated with S&P 500 declines over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5.5% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negatively correlated with UNRATE increases (p > 0.10 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in housing starts (HOUST > 1200) followed by two consecutive months above 1250 signals a revival in consumer confidence and supports positive S&P 500 momentum over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST crosses above 1250 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns show no significant positive relationship with the housing start surge (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) remains below its 52-week moving average for three consecutive months in a low-inflation regime, it predicts negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns due to persistent supply-side constraints.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 52-week MA for three consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 105
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when the supply constraint is not confirmed by actual output data (backtest failure).
